newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA'S TELKOM CUTS INTERNATIONAL CALL RATES.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA'S TELKOM CUTS INTERNATIONAL CALL RATES.

text.p: South Africa telecommunications utility Telkom said on Wednesday it would reduce international call rates to eight countries by as much as 20 percent with effect from April 1.
It said rates for calls to Germany, France, Netherlands, Austria, Italy, Greece, Hong Kong and Monaco would be reduced by between 6.7 and 20.2 percent.
The price cuts formed part of a process that would result in reduced rates to many other countries being phased in throughout the year, Telkom managing executive Rhynie Greeff said.
"This approach is necessary as Telkom has to negotiate the cost of international calls with its international telecommunications partners," he said.
Telkom is about to sign a deal which will give SBC Communications Inc and Telekom Malaysia Bhd a 30 percent stake in the concern.

The sale of the stake is expected to net around $1.3 billion rand, according to industry analysts, $1 billion of which will be ploughed back into Telkom to fund its infrastructure expansion programme.
